object_types.name: Account
object_types.definition: The customer entity in the system; every subscription hangs off an account.

source_references.excerpt: An account. Every account has an account number. That's what everything hangs off.

object_types.name: AccountNumber
object_types.definition: Unique six-digit sequential identifier for an account, never reused.

source_references.excerpt: Six digits, sequential, never reused.

object_types.name: Subscription
object_types.definition: The agreement that an account pays a given amount on a given cycle for a given product.

source_references.excerpt: A subscription is the agreement that this account pays us this amount on this cycle for this thing. It's got a subscription ID.

object_types.name: SubscriptionId
object_types.definition: Unique generated identifier for a subscription, prefixed with SUB.

source_references.excerpt: Unique. Generated, prefixed with SUB.

object_types.name: Product
object_types.definition: One of the company's products, fixed today at three.

source_references.excerpt: Product code. We have three: CORE, ANALYTICS, and CONNECT.

object_types.name: PricePlan
object_types.definition: The billing artefact that says what a customer pays and how often, generating the invoice line; identified by a plan code.

source_references.excerpt: The price plan. It's got a plan code, it says what the customer pays and how often. CORE-MO-49, CORE-AN-490, that kind of thing.

object_types.name: PlanCode
object_types.definition: Code identifying a price plan, e.g. CORE-MO-49.

source_references.excerpt: CORE-MO-49, CORE-AN-490, that kind of thing.

object_types.name: FeatureBundle

object_types.name: StartDate
object_types.definition: The date a subscription begins; always present, mandatory.

source_references.excerpt: Start date is always there. You can't create a subscription without one, the form won't submit.

object_types.name: EndDate
object_types.definition: The date a subscription ends; optional, only present for fixed-term or cancelled subscriptions.

source_references.excerpt: An open-ended subscription has no end date. ... A fixed-term one has an end date agreed up front

object_types.name: BillingPeriod
object_types.definition: The billing cycle of a subscription: monthly or annual.

source_references.excerpt: Monthly or annual.

object_types.name: SubscriptionStatus
object_types.definition: The status of a subscription: trialing, active, past due, cancelled.

source_references.excerpt: Trialing, active, past due, cancelled.

object_types.name: PausedFlag
object_types.definition: A separate boolean flag indicating a subscription is paused; overlaps confusingly with status.

source_references.excerpt: Paused isn't a status, it's a flag. ... it's a separate boolean, which is exactly why it causes bugs.

object_types.name: PlanChange
object_types.definition: A record of a change to a subscription's price plan, with an effective date and requester; belongs to exactly one subscription.

source_references.excerpt: A change is a record. We don't overwrite the plan on the subscription, we write a plan change with an effective date ... It's got a change ID.

object_types.name: ChangeId
object_types.definition: Unique identifier for a plan change.

source_references.excerpt: It's got a change ID.

object_types.name: EffectiveDate
object_types.definition: The date on which a plan change takes effect.

source_references.excerpt: it takes effect, and those are different dates ... It records the subscription, the new price plan, the effective date, and who requested it.

ambiguities.description: Three different concepts are all called 'plan' by different stakeholders: the billing PricePlan, the product FeatureBundle, and a sales-negotiated deal. The sales-negotiated 'deal' plan was explicitly mentioned but not modeled -- is it a distinct entity needing capture, or out of scope?

source_references.excerpt: We've got two things both called plan, and the sales team calls a third thing a plan, which is the deal they negotiated, which frequently matches neither.

ambiguities.description: Whether cancellation of a mid-term annual subscription should trigger a prorated refund, credit, or run-to-term is explicitly undecided business policy; the model captures only current system behavior (end date set to paid-through date, no refund mechanism). This may need revisiting once finance/legal decide.

source_references.excerpt: What happens commercially when an annual subscription is cancelled mid-term -- run to term, prorated refund, or credit -- is undecided.

ambiguities.description: The relationship between Subscription and its 'current' PricePlan: is it a denormalized/derived attribute maintained by the PlanChange process (as stated), or should the model only expose PlanChange history and derive current plan via query? The transcript states both a stored current-plan field AND that plan history should win in case of disagreement -- suggesting the stored field could become stale/buggy. Clarify whether current PricePlan should be modeled as stored or purely derived.

source_references.excerpt: No, Sam, it does have a current plan field. ... And if those two ever disagree, the change history wins and the current plan is the bug.

ambiguities.description: The paused flag overlaps with the four-value status enumeration in a way that is acknowledged to cause bugs (a paused subscription can still appear as 'active'). No constraint governs how PausedFlag interacts with SubscriptionStatus (e.g., can only Active subscriptions be paused?). This interaction needs clarifying.

source_references.excerpt: Paused isn't a status, it's a flag. ... If you ask the system for active subscriptions you get paused ones too.

ambiguities.description: MRR (monthly recurring revenue) is explicitly derived from PricePlan price and BillingPeriod and intentionally not modeled as a stored attribute; the exact formula (price normalized to a month) is given for annual (490/12=40.83) but the underlying PricePlan price value/currency field was never explicitly captured as a value type in the transcript, so the derivation cannot be precisely formalized without it.

source_references.excerpt: It's worked out. It's the plan price normalised to a month. An annual plan at 490 is an MRR of 40.83. ... So it's derived from the price plan and the billing period.

ambiguities.description: The FeatureBundle identifier is its Name, described by Tom as 'an ugly' identifier with 'no code, which annoys me' -- suggesting the business considers this identification scheme suboptimal though currently unique and workable. Confirm whether a future code-based identifier is expected, which would change the reference scheme.

source_references.excerpt: Name. Starter, Professional, Enterprise. There's no code, which annoys me.
